guide.title: Fields Ranch East: Golf in Frisco, Texas
guide.intro: Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Best in State ranking places PGA Frisco: Fields Ranch East eighth in Texas, labelled "Public" — the highest-ranked course in the state carrying that label; the seven courses ranked above it are each individually labelled "Private." Fields Ranch East is one of two courses on the Omni PGA Frisco Resort & Spa campus in Frisco, in Denton County. Gil Hanse and Jim Wagner designed it and it opened in May 2023. Fields Ranch West, the campus's other course, ranks twenty-second on the same list, also labelled "Public," and is a separate entry in this guide. This guide is about the course that placed eighth.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: By road, the course is 31.4 miles from Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW), via the Sam Rayburn Tollway (State Highway 121), the Dallas North Tollway, and Legacy Drive. From Dallas Love Field (DAL), it is 30.7 miles by road. The course's own coordinates and Golf Digest's own coordinates for it each geocode to Denton County (GEOID 48121) and to Frisco city (GEOID 4827684) on the US Census geocoder. Frisco itself spans two counties: Frisco City Hall, a separate site, geocodes to Collin County under the same Incorporated Place. The course's address is 3725 PGA Pkwy, Frisco, TX 75033.

sections.heading: Fields Ranch East
sections.body: Fields Ranch East opened in May 2023, designed by Gil Hanse and Jim Wagner. The operator's own site gives 18 holes, 7,863 yards, par 72, course rating 78.9, and slope 151. Golf Digest's course page states that the East course "has already hosted the KitchenAid Senior PGA Championship" and "is set to host... the PGA Championship (2027, 2034), the KPMG Women's PGA Championship (2025, 2031) and the KitchenAid Senior PGA Championship again in 2029." The operator's own East-course header separately calls it "Home of the 2027 PGA Championship." Dress code, per fieldsranch.com: "Golf shirts and closed-toe shoes are required on Fields Ranch East and Fields Ranch West, denim is not permitted."

sections.heading: Playing it: booking, price, and the caddie
sections.body: Fields Ranch East is public, not private: the PGA of America's own FAQ describes PGA Frisco as "a public/private partnership between the PGA of America, Omni Hotels & Resorts, the City of Frisco and the Frisco Independent School District," and no membership is required to book a tee time. Tee times run through the resort's own booking engine at omnipgafriscoexperiences.com, and how far ahead a golfer can book depends on who they are: the general public books 7 days ahead, Frisco residents book 10 days ahead, and registered guests of the Omni PGA Frisco Resort & Spa book up to 120 days ahead of their stay date. The public green fee is $350 per player — the rate the operator's own booking system quoted for every date of its public window during September 2026; resort-guest pricing for the same stretch of dates ran from $315 to $395 depending on the date. Fields Ranch East is a walking course with a mandatory caddie. Fieldsranch.com, read in September 2026, publishes CaddieMaster's own schedule: $80 plus tax per player for a double bag, $125 plus tax for a single bag from September through May, $110 plus tax for a single bag from June through August, and $40 to $120 plus tax per player for a forecaddie depending on group size. Caddie fees and gratuity are not included in the green fee, and the operator recommends a gratuity of $45 and up per bag for a walking caddie. Add a caddie fee to the green fee and a public round runs roughly $475 to $525 per player before gratuity. Carts are not generally available on Fields Ranch East: the operator's own seasonal restriction calendar bars them outright from March 27 through June 21 and again from September 18 through November 29, and in every other stretch of the year permits them only after a stated hour, often restricted to cart paths or ranch roads; push carts are never permitted.

sections.heading: Fields Ranch West
sections.body: Fields Ranch West, on the same campus, ranks twenty-second on the same Golf Digest Texas list, also labelled "Public." Beau Welling designed it. On the same date the operator's booking system quoted $350 for Fields Ranch East's public rate, it quoted $280 for Fields Ranch West's public rate, $260 for resort guests, and $252 for Frisco residents. Unlike the East course, carts are seasonally available on the West course with a forecaddie.

sections.heading: Staying and eating on the campus
sections.body: Golfers here typically stay at Omni PGA Frisco Resort & Spa, on the same campus as both courses. The resort's own site describes "500 comfortable guest rooms and suites," ten four-bedroom Ranch House Villas, and the Mokara Spa. Two dining outlets are named on the resort's own site: Ryder Cup Grille and Toast & Tee Coffee Collective. The resort's own golf page states: "Guests of Fields Ranch can access the Driving Range, Warm-Up Putting Green, and Chipping Green for same-day use prior to their tee time. These practice facilities are not open to the general public for use." Fieldsranch.com adds that weekly maintenance for the driving range is typically performed on Tuesdays.

faq.question: How do I book a tee time at Fields Ranch East?
faq.answer: Tee times run through the resort's own booking engine at omnipgafriscoexperiences.com. The general public can book 7 days ahead of a tee time, Frisco residents 10 days ahead, and registered guests of the Omni PGA Frisco Resort & Spa up to 120 days ahead of their stay date. The public green fee is $350 per player, the rate the operator's own booking system quoted for every date of its public window during September 2026. A caddie is mandatory for every player, at $80 to $125 plus tax depending on bag and season, or $40 to $120 plus tax for a forecaddie, so the realistic all-in cost of a public round is roughly $475 to $525 per player before gratuity.

faq.question: What does a round at Fields Ranch East cost?
faq.answer: $350 per player for the public green fee, the rate the operator's own booking system quoted for every date of its public window during September 2026; resort-guest pricing for the same stretch of dates ran from $315 to $395. A caddie is mandatory and is not included in that fee: $80 plus tax per player for a double bag, $125 plus tax for a single bag from September through May, $110 plus tax for a single bag from June through August, or $40 to $120 plus tax for a forecaddie, with a recommended gratuity of $45 and up per bag. All told, a public round runs roughly $475 to $525 per player before gratuity.

faq.question: Can I bring a cart?
faq.answer: Not generally. Fields Ranch East's own seasonal restriction calendar bars carts outright from March 27 through June 21 and again from September 18 through November 29, and in every other stretch of the year permits them only after a stated hour, often restricted to cart paths or ranch roads. Push carts are never permitted. A caddie is required for every player year-round. Fields Ranch West, the second course on the same campus, does allow seasonal cart use with a forecaddie.

faq.question: Where is the course, and what county is it in?
faq.answer: At the Omni PGA Frisco Resort & Spa campus, 3725 PGA Pkwy, Frisco, Texas. Both the finder's coordinates and Golf Digest's own coordinates for the course geocode to Denton County on the US Census geocoder. Frisco itself spans two counties — Frisco City Hall, a separate site, geocodes to Collin County — but the course sits on the Denton County side.

faq.question: Which second course is on the same campus?
faq.answer: Fields Ranch West, twenty-second on the same Golf Digest Texas list and also labelled "Public," designed by Beau Welling. Its public green fee was $280 on the same date Fields Ranch East's was $350, and carts are seasonally available there with a forecaddie.

places.name: Fields Ranch East
places.summary: Eighth on Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Best in State ranking for Texas, labelled "Public" — the highest-ranked course in the state carrying that label. Designed by Gil Hanse and Jim Wagner, it opened in May 2023: 18 holes, 7,863 yards, par 72, course rating 78.9, slope 151, per fieldsranch.com. It has hosted the KitchenAid Senior PGA Championship and is set to host the PGA Championship in 2027 and 2034, the KPMG Women's PGA Championship in 2025 and 2031, and the KitchenAid Senior PGA Championship again in 2029, per Golf Digest's own course page. It is a walking course with a mandatory caddie; the public green fee was $350 per player, observed across the operator's own booking system for every date of its public window during September 2026, with public tee times booked 7 days ahead.

places.name: Fields Ranch West
places.summary: Twenty-second on the same Golf Digest Texas ranking, also labelled "Public." Designed by Beau Welling, it shares the 660-acre campus with Fields Ranch East. On the same date the operator's booking system quoted $350 for Fields Ranch East's public rate, it quoted $280 for Fields Ranch West's public rate, $260 for resort guests, and $252 for Frisco residents. Carts are seasonally available on the West course with a forecaddie, unlike the East course.

places.name: Omni PGA Frisco Resort & Spa
places.summary: The resort at the center of the PGA Frisco campus, home to both Fields Ranch courses. Its own site describes "500 comfortable guest rooms and suites," ten four-bedroom Ranch House Villas, and the Mokara Spa. Registered resort guests may book tee times up to 120 days ahead of their stay date, well beyond the 7-day public booking window.
